Privacy Policy

This Privacy Policy describes how LEDGER ("we", "us", or "our") collects, uses, and shares your personal information when you use our financial management platform. We collect information you provide directly, including account metadata, financial transaction records, receipt attachments, and authentication tokens.

We use industry-standard military-grade encryption and secure connection protocols. Login events, important changes, and account connections are recorded in a secure log to keep your account safe and accountable.

  from?: string
  to?: string

  description?: string

}

  currentNetWorth: number
  monthlyIncome: number
  monthlyExpense: number
  savingsRate: number
  dailyBurnRate: number

}

  categoryId: string | null
  name: string
  color: string

  name: string
  totalCents: number
  count: number

export interface TrendPoint {
  date: string
  totalCents: number
}

export interface WeekdaySpend {
  dayOfWeek: number
  avgCents: number
  count: number

  categories: CategorySpend[]
  totalSpend: number
  topMerchants: MerchantTotal[]
  trend: TrendPoint[]

export interface BudgetCategory {
  id: string
  name: string
  icon: string | null
  color: string
  monthlyBudgetCents: number
  envelopeBalanceCents: number
  rolloverEnabled: boolean | null
  emergencyFund: boolean | null
  spendCents: number
  remainingCents: number
}

  budgets: BudgetCategory[]
  totalBudget: number
  totalSpend: number
  periodStart: string
  periodEnd: string
}

  month: string
  incomeCents: number
  expenseCents: number
}

  monthlyTotals: MonthlyCashFlow[]
  recurringCents: number
  oneTimeCents: number
  currentBalance: number
  dailySurplus: number

export interface CategoryDelta {
  name: string
  primaryCents: number
  compareCents: number
  changeCents: number
  changePct: number

  primaryPeriod: { from?: string; to?: string }

  compareExpenseCents: number
  primaryIncomeCents: number
  compareIncomeCents: number
  expenseChangePct: number
  incomeChangePct: number

}

export type ReportData = DashboardData | SpendingData | BudgetData | CashFlowData | CompareData

import React from 'react'; import { Box, Typography, Paper, Alert } from '@mui/material'; export default function AdminHelpArea() { return ( Admin Help & Architecture Guide This area contains sensitive infrastructure information and is restricted to administrators only. Entity Architectural Distinctions (Studios vs. Providers vs. Billers) Voyarr strictly decouples content creation, host scraping, and billing processing into three specialized entities:
  • Studios & Networks: Represents production companies and brand networks (e.g., Brazzers, MindGeek/Aylo). Manages metadata tagging, library organization, and parent/subsidiary network relationships.
  • Media Providers: Represents streaming sites and host targets (e.g., ManyVids, OnlyFans, Pornhub). Manages authentication credentials, browser session cookies, scraper rules, download quotas, and daily limits.
  • Subscription Billers: Represents payment processors listed on credit card statements (e.g., CCBill, Probiller, SegPay). Maps subscriptions to financial statement descriptors and tracks renewal dates.
 Internal File Storage & Write Paths Voyarr operates securely inside isolated Docker volumes. The backend will only attempt to write to the following designated directories:
  • /app/config/: System configurations, session states, and persistent certs.
  • /app/backups/: Used for automated JSON database backups.
  • /media/storage/logs/: FastAPI and Celery worker diagnostic logs.
  • /media/storage/downloads/: Ephemeral active queues and live stream recordings.
  • /tmp/: Used for temporary cookie text bridging to yt-dlp, Celery Beat lock files, and the Celery Beat schedule database (which prevents PUID write permission issues).
 VPN & Sidecar Architecture Gluetun VPN Sidecar: When using docker-compose.vpn.yml, all backend and worker containers are forced to route their network traffic through the Gluetun VPN container using network_mode: "service:vpn". Ensure you configure your VPN credentials correctly in .env.vpn before launching the stack, as an unhealthy VPN sidecar will block all external API and scraping requests. Tailscale Mesh VPN: For secure, remote access without exposing ports, you can deploy the docker-compose.tailscale.yml sidecar. It utilizes Tailscale Serve (via tailscale-serve.json) to automatically reverse proxy the Nginx frontend to your authorized private Tailnet nodes over HTTPS. You must provide a valid TS_AUTHKEY in your environment variables. Database, Routing & Port Troubleshooting Host Port Conflict Avoidance: Postgres (5432), Redis (6379), and the FastAPI backend (8000) are commented out on the host by default. The application is completely self-contained—the Nginx frontend reverse-proxies /api requests internally over Docker's bridge network. You only need to expose them if you explicitly connect external tools. Database Connection Refused: Ensure your DATABASE_URL strictly specifies port 5432. The backend must connect via the internal Docker bridge network, not your host's exposed Postgres port. Interactive API Docs 404: If the Swagger UI docs (/api/docs) return a 404, set ROOT_PATH=/api in your .env file. This informs FastAPI that it is running behind an Nginx prefix and correctly rewrites all internal asset URLs. Queue Starvation: If your Celery queues freeze during heavy scraping, increase CELERY_CONCURRENCY in your environment file and ensure Redis is healthy. Video Streaming & Media Serving SmartVideoPlayer: The built-in video player (SmartVideoPlayer component) auto-detects the playback strategy from each URL — HLS (.m3u8), MPEG-DASH (.mpd), or native HTML5 for all other container formats. The hls.js and dash.js libraries are loaded from CDN (jsdelivr.net / dashjs.org) on demand; no build-time dependency is added. Stream MIME Types: The backend's /api/library/{id}/stream endpoint detects the correct MIME type from the file extension and sets it in the Content-Type response header. This allows the browser to route the stream to the correct decoder. The following MIME types are handled: video/mp4, video/x-matroska (MKV), video/webm, video/quicktime (MOV), video/x-msvideo (AVI), video/x-ms-wmv, video/x-flv, video/mp2t (TS), video/mpeg, video/3gpp, and all common audio MIME types. Global Streaming Toggle: Streaming can be globally disabled by admins in Settings → Feature Permissions. When disabled, the player area displays a warning message instead of the video element. Users with insufficient role permissions to access streaming will receive a 403 Forbidden response, which does not trigger a logout — only 401 Unauthorized resets the session. Maximizing Compatibility: For guaranteed playback across all browsers (including Safari and mobile), use the Transcode Queue to convert files to MP4 with H.264 video and AAC audio. This format is natively supported by every modern browser without additional codec packs. Authentication & Session Management Passkey Setup Wizard: The onboarding wizard auto-populates the WebAuthn Relying Party ID (passkeys_rp_id) with the current window.location.hostname. The layout uses a responsive two-column grid on desktop/tablet screens. Default settings are pre-configured for standard server environments and do not require changes for most deployments. 401 vs. 403 Handling: The global API wrapper (api.js) and SSE stream handlers (App.jsx) only trigger a full session reset (redirect to login) on 401 Unauthorized responses. A 403 Forbidden response (e.g., RBAC restriction, feature disabled) is surfaced as an error in the UI without logging the user out. WebAuthn .well-known: The file at frontend/public/.well-known/webauthn lists the authorized Relying Party IDs that are allowed to use passkeys on this origin. Ensure the domain configured in passkeys_rp_id matches the origin from which users access the app. ); }

    •  For the widest browser support, use Settings → Transcode Queue to re-encode any file to MP4 (H.264 video + AAC audio).     }> How do live streams work in the player? The Live Streams tab resolves a monitored URL to its real stream link via the backend, then hands it off to the SmartVideoPlayer which auto-detects the protocol:
  • HLS (.m3u8) — Played via hls.js (all browsers) or natively (Safari/iOS). Low-latency mode is enabled.
  • MPEG-DASH (.mpd) — Played via dash.js, loaded from CDN on demand.
  • RTMP / RTSP — These protocols cannot play in a browser. The stream must be re-streamed as HLS (e.g., via FFmpeg or a server-side proxy) and the .m3u8 URL used instead.
    •  If the stream player shows "HLS not supported", ensure your browser has internet access to load hls.js from the CDN (jsdelivr.net).     }> Does Voyarr support VR headsets / WebXR immersive playback? Yes! The player has built-in **WebXR** rendering capabilities using Three.js (dynamic CDN lazy-loading):
  • Supported Headsets — Meta Quest (via Quest Browser), Apple Vision Pro (via Safari WebXR settings), HTC Vive, and all headsets supporting standard WebXR immersive VR sessions.
  • Projection Formats — Choose between **Flat Screen** (cinema theater mode), **180° Dome** (hemispherical projection), or **360° Sphere** (full spherical environment).
  • Stereoscopic Video — Supports stereoscopic Side-by-Side (SBS) videos. Enable **Stereo SBS** mode to map independent left/right perspectives to each eye.
  • Exiting VR Mode — Click the select/trigger button on either controller to exit immersive mode and return to the flat browser dashboard, or use your headset's system home button.
    •  If you do not see the "Enter Immersive VR" button, ensure you are accessing the dashboard over HTTPS or localhost, as WebXR is blocked by browsers on non-secure HTTP origins.     }> Can I browse my library in DeoVR Player without a password? Yes. Voyarr serves a native DeoVR-compatible scene feed. You can sign in from your VR headset by generating a temporary 6-digit pairing code — no password entry required on the headset.
  • On your desktop, go to Account Security → VR Headset & DeoVR Easy Sign-In → click Generate Code under "DeoVR Native Sign-In Code". A 6-digit code appears.
  • On your VR headset, open the DeoVR Player app and navigate to your Voyarr domain. Tap the Sign In button.
  • Enter the 6-digit code in the Password field. Leave the Username field blank.
  • Your library loads immediately in DeoVR's native VR interface — full metadata, thumbnails, and playback controls.
    •  The code expires after 5 minutes and can only be used once. Generate a new code from Account Security for each session. You can also use your Voyarr username and password directly in the DeoVR sign-in form.     }> What metadata does Voyarr expose to DeoVR? The DeoVR scene feed includes the following per-video metadata:
  • Title, description, date added — Basic video information from your library.
  • Performers, tags, categories — Media organization metadata for filtering and discovery.
  • Duration, rating — Video length and user-assigned rating.
  • VR projection — Stereo mode (SBS, top-bottom, off) and screen type (flat, 180°, 360°, fisheye) are auto-detected from metadata or filenames.
  • Video encodings — Multiple resolution options with direct stream URLs.
  • Thumbnails and gallery images — Cover art and additional screenshots.
  • Preview clips — Short preview video URLs when available.
  • Funscript / HSP — Haptic feedback file URLs for interactive devices.
  • Download sources — Direct download links for offline playback.
    •  The feed is paginated (50 items per page) and supports filtering by search query, studio, performer, or tag via URL parameters.     {/* ── Troubleshooting Tips ───────────────────────────────────────── */} Troubleshooting Tips
    • If tasks are stuck in "Pending", ensure the Celery Worker container is running and healthy.
    • If metadata isn't saving to files, verify your /media/storage volume mapping points to the correct host folder.
    • For UI rendering issues, try clearing your browser cache or adjusting the Theme in Interface Preferences.
    • If a video shows a codec error, use the Transcode Queue to convert it to MP4 (H.264 + AAC) for maximum browser compatibility.
    • If a live stream shows "HLS not supported" or fails to load, ensure your browser has internet access to load hls.js from cdn.jsdelivr.net.
    • If you encounter database lock errors during bulk operations, check your disk I/O performance and ensure the SQLite database is not on a network drive.
    • If thumbnails fail to generate, check that the FFmpeg binary is accessible within the container and verify your media file permissions.
